structured.approach: I used the FE-03 procedure from the frontend-steps skill. First I read the contracted inputs: feat.tasks, feat.stories, feat.design and task.repo_access in full, and the frontend-relevant parts of feat.prd and feat.trd (IF-7, F-12 to F-14, T-12 to T-16, AC-19 to AC-21, NFR-3/7/10). Then I read the whole ap_portal checkout with Read and Glob: index.js, portal.test.js, package.json, ci.mjs, README.md and CLAUDE.md. That gave me the existing layer, exports, callers and CI rules. I mapped the TSK-07 / feat.design B4 components onto the single existing view-helper module and picked the smallest additive change. Everything stays in index.js: one new export, private helpers, two constants, a version step and new tests, with no new file or layer. The verifier subagent had checked the earlier content against its sources. In this rewrite I took out the unsupported statement about how the code was read and kept only facts the sources support. I did not use codegraph, because the repository is one small module plus one test file and I read all of it directly.

claims.text: ap_portal has a single source module, src/ap_portal/index.js. It exports VERSION, LABELS, formatAmount and renderAgingSummary. VERSION is '2.3.0', the same as package.json.
formatAmount formats through Number(...).toFixed(2), which is a float, against D-2026-044. The new renderer must not reuse it, and it stays unchanged (TQ-2).

The components to add, all in src/ap_portal/index.js: the constants RISK_CLASSES and OVERDUE_HEADINGS, the private helpers escapeHtml, toTwoDecimalString and riskClass, and the exported renderOverdueRisk added to module.exports.

renderOverdueRisk returns '' for undefined, null or []. It throws TypeError for other non-array rows, for a non-integer days and for an amount that is not a decimal string. It renders a plain header row and one risk-class row per input row, in the given order.
VERSION in index.js and "version" in package.json take one minor step together from 2.3.0. The exact number is for the lane to confirm.
New node:test cases go in tests/portal.test.js (the feat.design B4.5 list plus the feat.tasks coverage cases). The two existing tests stay unchanged.
CI runs node --check and node:test with NODE_PATH=src, requires line coverage of src/** of at least 90, and fails on console.log, eval( or lines over 140 characters.
No new module, layer, stylesheet, transport or host-page change is needed. A transport would re-trigger DES-01.
The repository is available with write access on branch feature/story. Neither a database nor Databricks is used.

open_questions: CQ-FE-1 (non-blocking, Architect): CT-1 types id and vendor as strings, but no input says what renderOverdueRisk should do with a missing or non-string id or vendor. The design's escapeHtml(String(value)) would render the text 'undefined'. Should it throw TypeError instead, as it does for amount and days (DD-8)? Until answered, I follow feat.design B4.2.
CQ-FE-2 (non-blocking, UX lead): Who styles the overdue-risk table and the risk-* row classes? ap_portal has no stylesheet, and the host page is out of scope for this design.
Carried, non-blocking: TQ-2, TQ-6, TQ-7, TQ-11, OQ-B8, OQ-B9, OQ-B10; RA-1 (branch name feature/story vs feature/<story>) and RA-2 (remote write access not yet tested).
structured.summary: I rewrote task.components in full for FE-03, covering TSK-07 (STORY-07) in ap_portal. The smallest change is additive and stays inside the existing view-helper module src/ap_portal/index.js. It adds the constants RISK_CLASSES and OVERDUE_HEADINGS, the private helpers escapeHtml, toTwoDecimalString and riskClass, and the exported renderOverdueRisk added to module.exports. It also takes a minor version step in both index.js and package.json, and adds new node:test cases to tests/portal.test.js. LABELS, formatAmount (float path, TQ-2), renderAgingSummary, the existing tests, ci.mjs, the host page and the transport all stay unchanged. The file also covers the CT-1 input contract, the CI constraints and traceability to the stories, the TRD and the design. I removed the unsupported statement about how the code was read. There are two non-blocking questions: whether a missing id or vendor should throw, and who styles the risk classes. No blocking questions.
